claims.text: Rapid solidification of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will produce a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will achieve a room-temperature yield strength of at least 1345 MPa.
The processed alloy will achieve at least 38% compressive fracture strain or more than 15% tensile elongation at room temperature.
The alloy density will be significantly below 8.0 g/cm³.
The density target is approximately 8.5-9.0 g/cm³ or lower and below that of traditional Ni-based superalloys.
Cast equiatomic or near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr initially has a continuous B2 matrix or substantial segregation that causes brittleness.
Solutionizing near 1400°C will form a single-phase disordered BCC structure.
Aging at approximately 600-800°C will precipitate discrete nanoscale B2 phases in the BCC matrix.
Selective laser melting or melt spinning can kinetically trap a metastable BCC matrix with fine B2 precipitates.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix increases dislocation mobility and strain hardening and thereby prevents premature cleavage.
Discrete B2 precipitates maintain high yield strength through precipitate cutting or Orowan looping.
The Hf-Zr-Ti combination stabilizes B2 at lower volume fractions than in Al-rich systems.
Mo and Ta provide solid-solution strengthening in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Eliminating or minimizing Al reduces alloy density relative to Al-containing RHEAs.
Eliminating or minimizing Al avoids formation of a continuous brittle B2 network.
Conventional cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr or similar RHEAs generally fail below 5% strain or otherwise lack a useful strength-ductility combination.
B2 volume fractions above approximately 30-40 vol% will percolate and restore brittle behavior.
The processing window is bounded by an order-disorder transition temperature and by the onset of excessive grain growth or precipitate coarsening.
Processing must use an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation of the refractory elements.
The alloy will exhibit anomalous strengthening at 600°C because of complex slip systems in the B2 precipitates.

contradictions.description: The density is said to be significantly below 8.0 g/cm³ while the stated target is approximately 8.5-9.0 g/cm³; these numerical targets are mutually inconsistent.

The claimed strength target is above 1300 MPa, specifically at least 1345 MPa, but the experiment only falsifies the strength claim below 1000 MPa, leaving results from 1000 to 1344 MPa that fail the prediction without triggering falsification.

The predicted density is below 8.0 g/cm³, whereas density falsification is set only above 9.5 g/cm³ or relative to the cast baseline, leaving a broad range that misses the prediction but is not declared falsifying.
